body.statement: On \(\mathcal B_n\), given the validated oracle \(\mathcal O_n\) for the clipped fields, if \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}+w_n<0\), clipping is inactive and the exhaustive procedure in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}negative\text{-}certificate}\) terminates. Its output \(\mathcal C_{pq,n}\) contains rational \(u_0,z,t_{\mathrm{ch}}\) with \(u_0,u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z\in\operatorname{int}(\Omega)\), two outward-rounded interval enclosures for the population increments \(F_p(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_p(u_0)\) and \(F_q(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_q(u_0)\), and a rational upper bound strictly below zero for their inner product. Hence \[\langle F_q(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_q(u_0),F_p(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_p(u_0)\rangle<0,\] so \(C_{q\leftarrow p}\) is not Euclidean monotone.
body.justification: The proposition turns a negative band endpoint into an explicitly represented, checkable chord using a stated oracle and a population enclosure derived from the Hessian band.
body.gap: The located Brenier estimation and multivariate-rank papers report norm loss or distributional tests, not a terminating interval certificate for a causal cross-regime monotonicity violation.
body.consumer: Model auditors receive a reproducible rational chord, validated population increment enclosures, and a strict sign certificate rather than only a scalar rejection.
